content: 1. The purpose of WikiDoc is to establish a high-quality, free-content medical encyclopedia that fosters collaboration and mutual respect among contributors. The platform must not be used for advocacy, propaganda, or external conflicts. Contributors acting against these objectives, even with good intentions, may be asked to stop. 2. WikiDoc is a reference resource, not a battleground. All users are expected to interact civilly, calmly, and cooperatively. Personal attacks and edit wars are strictly prohibited. Editors unable to resolve personal or ideological disputes should minimize contact. If they fail to disengage, restrictions may be imposed. 3. Source material must be represented accurately and fairly. Quoting or citing a source implies that the material reflects the original source's meaning without being misleading or taken out of context. Misrepresentation of sources, whether intentional or accidental, undermines the encyclopedia's integrity and may result in sanctions. 4. Editors with single-purpose accounts or strong personal views on a topic must contribute neutrally and avoid creating the impression of bias. Non-neutral editing is incompatible with WikiDoc's goals. 5. Users are expected to behave reasonably, courteously, and calmly. Personal attacks, incivility, bad-faith assumptions, harassment, and disruptive behavior are prohibited. Accusations of misconduct must not be made without evidence, especially if done repeatedly or in bad faith. 6. Users sanctioned for improper conduct must avoid repeating such behavior. Continued violations may result in increasingly severe sanctions. 7. All WikiDoc articles must maintain a neutral point of view, representing all relevant perspectives proportionally. Undue emphasis on peripheral aspects is not allowed. Original research and synthesized claims are prohibited. Articles must not be used for advocacy or promotion. 8. Assume good faith when interacting with others. Treat others as you would like to be treated. Be polite and mindful of how your words may be perceived, as text lacks tone and body language. Register yourself and sign your posts on talk pages. 9. Work toward agreement by focusing on facts rather than personalities. Address questions and provide reasons for your edits. Concede points when necessary and remain civil, even in heated discussions. 10. Recognize your biases and give credit where it is due. Help mediate disputes and take breaks if arguments become heated. If mediation is needed, enlist someone to assist. 11. Avoid reverting or deleting edits unless necessary, and explain your reasons in the edit summary. Remember that you are dealing with real people who deserve dignity and respect. 12. Review the vandal's contributions for additional malicious edits and leave warning messages on their talk page. 13. To undo vandalism, access the page history, select the correct version, and edit the page. Verify that you are reverting to the last clean version and provide a brief explanation in the comments. Check the vandal's contribution history and report them if necessary. 14. Warning templates are available for addressing vandalism. Use them appropriately, escalating warnings as needed. Severe or repeated vandalism may result in the user being blocked from editing. 15. Trace the IP address of vandals using tools like ARIN, RIPE, or APNIC. Add the owner's name to the vandal's talk page if applicable. 16. Common types of vandalism include blanking, spamming, using bots for mass vandalism, adding graffiti, creating joke articles, inserting misinformation, and altering links or templates. Other forms include offensive page moves, redirecting to inappropriate content, and uploading provocative images. 17. Not all disruptive behavior is vandalism. Examples include testing the editing feature, learning wiki markup, accidental NPOV violations, bold edits, and honest mistakes. These actions should be addressed with guidance rather than punishment. 18. WikiDoc has a clear policy against personal attacks and harassment. While some forms of harassment overlap with vandalism, they are generally treated as separate issues. 19. Be cautious when uploading copyrighted images. Always tag images with appropriate copyright information, specify their source, and provide detailed descriptions. Use high-resolution images when possible and follow format guidelines for different types of content. 20. Policies are enforced by users through editing and discussion. Administrators may impose temporary blocks for vandalism or other violations. In extreme cases, the Arbitration Committee may intervene. 21. Certain features, such as page deletion and protection, are restricted to administrators. These actions must align with protection and blocking policies. 22. Additional guidelines include signing posts, avoiding profanity, being accountable, welcoming newcomers, using user pages appropriately, and applying common sense.
